readme.name: README
rows: 9 compounds (Level 1: 1, Level 2a: 2, Level 2b: 1, Level 3: 5; 1 anthropogenic contaminants) detected in 2 samples (Site A, Site B); 1 excluded identities in sheet Excluded.
Synthetic test campaign (fixture, not real data). Fictional Orbitrap, DDA fictional HCD, ESI+ and ESI-; two solid-phase extraction sorbents per sample (OA, EC).

A compound is present at a sample when one of its features is DETECTED by MZmine with an area ≥ 5 x its abundance in the procedural blanks (or absent from them) (either sorbent; gap-filled values are never detections). n = 1 per site: no statistical test.
Progressive number: anthropogenic contaminants first, then by confidence level, then by name.
Curated common name of the identity (one row per compound; synonyms, brand names and library codes of the same compound merged).
Identification confidence after Schymanski et al. (Environ. Sci. Technol. 2014, 48, 2097): 1, 2a or 3 (criteria below). The best level among the features of the compound.
anthropogenic contaminant (curated list of contaminants of emerging concern and industrial chemicals) or not classified as anthropogenic (not in that list; this is not a claim of natural origin).

Acute aquatic hazard category of the structure, CLP Annex I Table 4.1.0 with the GHS (UN) thresholds on the lowest acute L(E)C50 among fish (96 h LC50), crustaceans (48 h EC50) and algae or aquatic plants (72-96 h ErC50 / EC50): Acute 1 (<= 1 mg/L), Acute 2 (> 1 to 10 mg/L), Acute 3 (> 10 to 100 mg/L), Not classified (> 100 mg/L or no effects at saturation); Not assessable = no structure or no data. Acute 2 and 3 exist in the UN GHS, not in the EU CLP. A hazard class, not a risk: the areas are signals, not concentrations.

Source tier of the acute category; the first tier with a category decides: regulatory (CLP harmonised classification), measured (L(E)C50 from the US EPA ECOTOX Knowledgebase, laboratory tests, geometric mean per species, or curated literature values), notified classification (H-statements of PubChem's GHS section: ECHA C&L notifications and other classifiers), predicted (curated read-across, else US EPA ECOSAR 2.2 class-based QSAR; baseline narcosis only = lower bound), not assessable.
The data that decided the acute category: taxon, species, endpoint, duration, value (mg/L) and number of results, the H-statements, the ECOSAR classes and predicted values, or the curated basis.

Chronic (long-term) aquatic hazard category, CLP Annex I Table 4.1.0: from chronic NOEC/EC10 (Chronic 1 <= 0.1, Chronic 2 <= 1 mg/L), else from acute L(E)C50 (Chronic 1 <= 1, 2 <= 10, 3 <= 100 mg/L), the more stringent when chronic data miss a trophic level (CLP 4.1.3.3); Chronic 4 = safety net or notified H413. The substance is assumed NOT rapidly degradable (no degradability data used): a worst case for degradable compounds.
Source tier of the chronic category (as for the acute one; predicted chronic values are ECOSAR chronic values, ChV).
The data that decided the chronic category, with the route (chronic data, acute data, or both).

Limits of the hazard record: Level 3 (hazard of the CSI:FingerID candidate, an isomer may differ), RT isomer (hazard of the named structure), a predicted category contradicted by a notified classification.
What the lower tiers say when they disagree with the category given (tier and category).
Neutral molecular formula of the structure (ASCII).
Monoisotopic mass of the molecular formula (Da).

InChIKey of the structure given by the source that named the compound; when that source gives only the connectivity block (14 characters), the full key of the PubChem representative structure. LC-HRMS does not determine stereochemistry: compare on the first block.
Source of the structure: the source that named the compound (reference standard, CSI:FingerID, SIRIUS spectral, GNPS2, mzMine library) or PubChem name (resolution of the name, weaker).
Ionisation mode of the representative ion (the feature with the best evidence at the compound's level).
Ion type of the representative ion, as given by the evidence source (inferred from m/z when the source gives none: see Flags).
Measured m/z of the representative ion.
Retention time of the representative ion (min).
Retention time of the best-evidence feature of the identity (min): one identity is one compound at one retention time.
Lowest and highest retention time of the features collapsed in the row (min).
(measured m/z - theoretical m/z of the adduct of the molecular formula) / theoretical m/z x 10^6 (ppm).
Sources whose evidence passed the criteria of the compound's level, over all its features at that level.
Library of the best spectral match (Level 2a, and Level 3 resting on a library match), the reference standard (Level 1) or CSI:FingerID (Level 3).
Identifier of the matched library spectrum (GNPS2 CCMSLIB ID or USI), or the name of the reference standard.
Cosine similarity of the best spectral-library match of the representative ion (Level 2a, and Level 3 resting on a library match).
Fragment ions shared with the library spectrum (for MZmine, its own count of matching signals).
COSMIC confidence score of the CSI:FingerID candidate of the representative ion (Level 3).
Level 1: m/z error against the reference standard (ppm).
Level 1: retention-time difference from the reference standard on the same instrument (min).
Level 1: cosine of the MS/MS spectrum against the reference standard's spectrum of the same ion.
Level 1: fragment ions matched with the reference standard's spectrum.

yes if at least one Level 1-3 feature of the compound is present in the sample Site A: DETECTED by MZmine with an area ≥ 5 x its abundance in the procedural blanks (or absent from them) (either sorbent; gap-filled values are never detections).

yes if at least one Level 1-3 feature of the compound is present in the sample Site B: DETECTED by MZmine with an area ≥ 5 x its abundance in the procedural blanks (or absent from them) (either sorbent; gap-filled values are never detections).
Largest peak area among the features of the compound present in Site A (larger of the two sorbents). Arbitrary units: a signal, not a concentration; not comparable between compounds.
Largest peak area among the features of the compound present in Site B (larger of the two sorbents). Arbitrary units: a signal, not a concentration; not comparable between compounds.
yes if at least one feature of the compound is present in a OA extract at any site (same rule).
yes if at least one feature of the compound is present in a EC extract at any site (same rule).
Largest number of procedural blanks in which a feature of the compound was found (MZmine blank subtraction).

Smallest, over the sites where the compound is DETECTED (blanks ignored), of (largest DETECTED area at the site / largest abundance of its features in the procedural blanks). Empty when the compound is absent from every blank.
Robust above 5x blank at all sites

Only for compounds DETECTED at all sites when the blanks are ignored: yes if at every site at least one DETECTED feature has an area ≥ 5 x its procedural-blank abundance (or is absent from the blanks); no = within 5x the blank at ≥ 1 site.
yes if at least one feature is DETECTED in the control sample None with an area ≥ 5 x its procedural-blank abundance (same rule as the sites).
CANOPUS (SIRIUS) ClassyFire superclass predicted for the representative feature, shown only with probability ≥ 0.70.
CANOPUS (SIRIUS) NPClassifier pathway predicted for the representative feature, shown only with probability ≥ 0.70.
Number of features (ions, adducts, polarities, in-source fragments) collapsed into the compound.
The features of the compound: polarity and MZmine row ID in the aligned feature tables.

In-house reference standard measured on the same instrument and LC method: precursor m/z within 5 ppm, RT within 0.35 min of the standard, and MS/MS cosine ≥ 0.70 on ≥ 2 matched fragments against the standard's own spectrum of the same ion (MS/MS tolerance 0.01 Da). Borderline MS/MS cases are decided by the analyst on the mirror plot (flagged).

Spectral-library match: cosine ≥ 0.70 and ≥ 4 matched fragment ions, for every library (SIRIUS spectral library, GNPS2, MZmine), with the library precursor within 15 ppm (GNPS2) or 15 ppm (MZmine) of the feature (analogue hits excluded). A match below these gates is not evidence: it gives neither a level nor a name. Level 2a resting on the MZmine library alone is flagged for the reader.

Structure supported by diagnostic evidence: a reference spectrum of the same structure that matches on diagnostic fragments (also below the Level 2a gates), or a fragment specific of the structure, judged by the analyst on the MS/MS spectrum and recorded per feature with the evidence (library entry, cosine, matched ions); never assigned automatically. An analogue match (reference precursor shifted by a mass difference) is never Level 2a; it supports 2b only with the diagnostic fragments confirmed on the raw spectrum. Reported apart from Level 2a and counted with Level 2 in the totals.

The features of an identity (same curated name, both polarities, same LC) are grouped by retention time: consecutive features more than 0.20 min apart are different peaks. The group with the best evidence (level, number of valid sources, sites, area) keeps the name; the others are reported as '<name> isomer, RT x.x min'. When two groups rest on a library match of the same compound the spectrum does not tell the isomers apart and all of them are Level 3; when the reference standard (Level 1) fixes the retention time, a library match at another retention time is Level 3 (another isomer).

Tentative structure: CSI:FingerID candidate with COSMIC confidence ≥ 0.64 (about 10% false discovery rate; Hoffmann et al., Nat. Biotechnol. 2022, 40, 411); or a Level 2a library match downgraded because the valid library matches of the same feature name structures with different connectivity (different InChIKey first blocks), or because the analyst judged it insufficient (both flagged).
A reference standard matching precursor m/z and RT whose MS/MS could not confirm it is a suspect, not an identification: it is not in this table.
No procedural-blank / control-sample audit was supplied: the control columns are empty.

Level 2a feature(s) whose only library match above threshold is MZmine (no second library confirms it); '(n of m Level 2a features)' when the compound has other Level 2a features. Information for the reader.
Level 3: library matches of different structures, not told apart by the spectrum

Level 2a downgraded to 3: two or more spectral libraries pass every gate but name structures with different connectivity, and the best match exceeds the best match of another structure by less than 0.05 in cosine (the cosines of the three tools are different functions; a smaller difference does not tell the structures apart). The name shown is the one of the best match.
libraries name different structures: the best match names the compound

Two or more spectral libraries pass every gate but name structures with different connectivity: the libraries are treated as one library and the best match (highest cosine, then more shared fragment ions) names the compound. It stays Level 2a when it exceeds the best match of another structure by at least 0.05 in cosine, otherwise Level 3 (see the previous flag). The competing matches and the margin are listed in brackets.
Level 3: library match judged insufficient by the analyst
Level 2a downgraded to 3 by the analyst after review of the spectra.

the name covers isomers that MS/MS does not tell apart (a curated union named after the formula class, e.g. 'disaccharide (sucrose/palatinose)'), an oligomer series grouped by molecular formula (PEG/polyether), the features of the compound point to structures with different connectivity (different InChIKey first blocks), or the same library compound matched peaks at different retention times (Level 3). Stereoisomers are never distinguished (see InChIKey).
Level 3: library match at a retention time other than the reference standard's (another isomer)
Level 2a downgraded to 3: the reference standard (Level 1) elutes at another retention time, so this peak is another isomer.
the same name at another retention time is a separate identity
features with the same name elute at other retention times: they are reported as separate identities ('<name> isomer, RT x.x min').
Level 3: the retention time is inconsistent with the predicted logP of the candidate relative to the other candidates of the batch (isotonic fit, robust z-score): a warning, not a rejection.
Level 3 candidate reviewed by hand against the lower-ranked CSI:FingerID candidates and RT.
Level 1 confirmed by the analyst on the MS/MS mirror plot
Level 1 whose MS/MS match was borderline and was confirmed by the analyst on the mirror plot.
the evidence source gives no ion type: the common adduct closest to the measured m/z is reported.
DETECTED within Nx procedural blank at: ...
DETECTED at those sites, but no feature above N x the procedural blank: not counted as present there.
Level 2b: structure supported by diagnostic evidence, judged by the analyst on the MS/MS spectrum
the compound rests on Level 2b features only: the analyst's decision on diagnostic evidence (criteria above).
